It’s a full slate of economic data and earnings as the Fed starts its two-day meeting. 

September economic reports include durable goods orders and new home sales. October reports include Conference Board consumer confidence and the Richmond Fed manufacturing and Dallas Fed services surveys. For August, we get the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller and FHFA home price indexes. We’ll also get the weekly ADP NER Pulse.

The FOMC begins its two-day meeting, with the decision Wednesday at 2pm ET.

41 S&P 500 components report, six of them with market caps over $100B:

Before the open: Coca-Cola ($KO), Boeing ($BA), S&P Global ($SPGI), HCA Healthcare ($HCA), Freeport-McMoRan ($FCX), American Tower ($AMT), Johnson Controls ($JCI), UPS ($UPS), Sherwin-Williams ($SHW), Ecolab ($ECL), Hilton ($HLT), Illinois Tool Works ($ITW), Royal Caribbean ($RCL), Paccar ($PCAR), PayPal ($PYPL), IQVIA ($IQV), CenterPoint Energy ($CNP), Xylem ($XYL), Hubbell ($HUBB), CMS Energy ($CMS), Invesco ($IVZ) and Pentair ($PNR)
After the close: Visa ($V), Seagate Technology ($STX), Waste Management ($WM), Robinhood ($HOOD), Oneok ($OKE), NXP Semiconductors ($NXPI), Baker Hughes ($BKR), Ventas ($VTR), EQT ($EQT), Arch Capital ($ACGL), Extra Space Storage ($EXR), FirstEnergy ($FE), F5 ($FFIV), PPG Industries ($PPG), Expand Energy ($EXE), Essex Property Trust ($ESS), CoStar Group ($CSGP), Universal Health Services ($UHS) and BXP ($BXP)

Outside the US, Novartis ($NVS) and Porsche ($DRPRY) also report, followed by SK Hynix ($SKHY) in the evening.

Ex-US highlights include China September industrial profits, South Korea Q3 GDP, France October consumer confidence, Eurozone September M3 and the ECB’s Q3 Bank Lending Survey. Israel also holds parliamentary elections.

Despite all the headwinds, German business leaders are the most optimistic about the future since early 2022, and they’ve been pretty good forecasters of where things are headed boding well for the German economy.

▪ Business climate rose to 90.2 from 89.9, the highest since May 2023 and a sixth straight monthly gain
▪ Expectations rose to 91.6 from 90.4, the highest since February 2022
▪ Current situation slipped to 88.8 from 89.5
▪ Manufacturing climate turned positive (+1.2), the highest since April 2023

Since 2005, ifo expectations have led German real GDP growth by about two quarters, according to Claude’s analysis (correlation 0.71 excluding 2020–21, 0.58 across all quarters). The current-situation level, as you might expect, is more of a coincident indicator, moving with GDP rather than ahead of it.

And since 2022, German firms have been gloomier than the GDP data, arguing for an even stronger reading. Measured against the pre-pandemic relationship, growth has run about 3.5 percentage 
points above what the expectations level implied.

What has been more consistent is the year-over-year change in the business climate. It has tracked GDP growth two quarters ahead with a 0.84 correlation excluding 2020–21, and 0.74 since 2022. October’s climate is 2.3 points above last year’s fourth-quarter average. On that relationship, that lines up with German GDP growth of roughly 2% year over year in Q2 2027, versus 1.0% in Q2 2026.

Replit's Amjad Masad with Gagan Biyani on how agents will reshape the way companies work: bureaucracy runs in the background, people get true autonomy, and eventually the company runs itself.

Amjad: "In Silicon Valley there's been so many experiments to try to change the nature of firms, of how companies work... But I think it was a technology problem."

"Now you can have agents kind of function as the glue within these organizations and have the bureaucracy be this invisible thing that's happening by machines in the background, and the people have true autonomy to work on the things that they find most interesting."

"I see it in our company where I've changed how I run the company, and we call it this idea of a self-driving company. Eventually the company will run itself."

Gagan: "The thing I feel very certain about is it's all gonna change. It's gonna change a lot faster than you think. And if you're not natively understanding of it, it's gonna be hard to make that shift."

Amjad: "If you're learning the ways of the past, then you're kind of locked into a way of thinking and a way of working that actually will put you at a fundamental disadvantage in the future."

@amasad @Replit @GaganBiyani

- Offshore outsourced talent: ~$10
- US back-office labor: $30-45

The yen carry trade is still running the show in emerging markets.

Borrow yen near zero, buy high-yielding Latin American currencies, pocket the spread. On October 26 almost the entire region gained against the yen, from the Chilean peso up 0.93% to the Mexican peso up 0.86%. Even a brutal 7.69% drop in the Brazilian real did not break the trade.

This is the plumbing of global risk. When the yen snaps back and the unwind starts, it does not stay in Brazil. It lands on everything, US stocks included. For now it is holding. Watch the yen.

MSFT's last voluntary retirement offer saw ~30% acceptance. This one is broader and MSFT expects a lower take rate; call it 10% for a conservative case = $2.4B/year in ongoing savings.
